description: The workflow skeleton a bare process draft needs before it accepts ANY further write — a freshly created process PUTs 500 even completely unmodified until ProcessDef/Activities exist.
notes: WorkflowType:"Sequence" means the ORDER of ProcessDef::Activity IS the flow — there are no edge nodes for the forward path (GotoTask, in goto_task.json, is the one exception: a backward jump).
Model::Appearance -> Appearance -> Style must exist on every flow (any FlowType) or the builder page fails to render with a bare "There was an error" — the write API itself never requires it.
Button::Row is a Row every human-built process carries (Button:<model id> instead of the usual Row/Column back-refs) — omitting it is accepted by the API but diffs from every UI-built process.
Assignees (Activity::Resource, ValueType:AppRole) CANNOT be written before the process has members — publish fails with a bare MetadataError if attempted first. Members first, assignees second.

SendBackToInitiator (a special node with Name:null) is a normal, expected sibling of the chain on a real process — not shown here since this shape focuses on the minimum skeleton, but its absence is not itself a defect.
